title: Machine learning reveals disruptive nutrient pollution shifts in Chinese rivers to 2100
abstract: Abstract Anticipating nutrient pollution under changing conditions is urgent for water security. Nonetheless, high-resolution predictive frameworks capturing nonlinear driver responses remain limited. Here, we present a nationwide assessment of China’s water-quality evolution from 2023 to 2100, integrating over 3 million daily records with 41 climatic, landscape, and socioeconomic drivers via regionally tailored Random Forest models ( R 2 of 0.88–0.92). Our results reveal a disruptive spatiotemporal shift, with projected NPI ranges from –50.9% to +218.1% under SSP5-8.5. Seasonal patterns restructure toward unimodal peaks, with pollution increases in spring/autumn (up to 28.3%) but decreases in summer (up to 27.0%). Spatial homogenization emerges via a westward/southward shift of pollution centers, with localized increases exceeding 200% from coldspots with low baselines (<0.4 vs >1.0 in hotspots). Landscape configuration dominates (64.5% feature importance) over climatic forcing (7.2%–35.5%), reinforced by minimal climatic projection uncertainty. Strategic land-use planning could be a cornerstone of future water security.
field: Machine learning prediction of nutrient pollution
problem: Existing high-resolution predictive frameworks for nutrient pollution are limited, as they struggle to capture the nonlinear responses to interacting climatic, landscape, and socioeconomic drivers, thus failing to anticipate disruptive future shifts in pollution patterns.
method: We propose a novel analytical framework that integrates nationwide daily monitoring data with explainable machine learning to quantify and project the future spatiotemporal dynamics of nutrient pollution in China’s rivers.
task: The task is to project future nutrient pollution shifts in Chinese rivers to 2100 using a machine learning framework that integrates nationwide water quality data with climatic, landscape, and socioeconomic drivers.
innovation: This paper presents an explainable machine learning framework that projects a disruptive westward and southward shift in China's nutrient pollution to 2100, identifying landscape configuration as a more dominant driver than climate factors.

kg_extraction_triplets.paragraph: Daily water quality parameters, including total nitrogen (TN), total phosphorus (TP), ammonia nitrogen (NH3-N), chemical oxygen demand (COD), water temperature (WT), and dissolved oxygen (DO), were sourced from the Ministry of Ecology and Environment of China (MEEC). These parameters were selected for their relevance in characterizing nutrient-related basin pollution 43, 62. Our analysis used 2023 as the baseline, a strategic choice that ensured temporal alignment between water quality and potential driving factors (e.g., climatic, land-use, and socioeconomic variables for 2023) while capturing the most recent, representative state of nutrient pollution. There are 1606 monitoring stations nationwide, offering extensive spatial and temporal coverage (Fig. 1). Nevertheless, some areas, particularly in the west and at high altitudes, exhibit relatively sparse coverage (Fig. S30). According to MEEC, these indicators were measured at automatic monitoring stations according to the national standard methods for the examination of water and wastewater 26, 63.
